nodes.description:
## Why

Found by the P3 exit gate (OWL-212, 2026-10-13). OWL-256's fix run started at 17:18:46 and ended at 17:59:30 by the event log's timestamps, 40.7 minutes, but its `run_ended` event says `elapsed_ms=918556`, 15.3 minutes: the machine slept during the run, and the monotonic clock behind `elapsed_ms` does not count sleep on macOS. Times read from `elapsed_ms`, such as the exit gates' records, under-report what the operator waited.

## Scope

* Keep `elapsed_ms` (monotonic, which deadlines rely on) and add the wall-clock span between `run_started` and `run_ended`, or document that `elapsed_ms` excludes sleep where the event format is described.
* Say in the build plan which one the gates' records use.

## Acceptance

* A run across a sleep shows both durations, or the event format says which one it records and why.
nodes.title: Record a run's wall-clock time next to its monotonic elapsed time

## Why

Roadmap P4, "The drain": Owlshift picks its own work, one ticket at a time. The design ([OWL-244](https://linear.app/owlshift/issue/OWL-244), pull request #215) splits the work into parts A to L; this issue is part **L · The exit gate,**. The rules are settled there, so this issue does not decide them again.

## Scope

The procedure is the build plan's "P4 tasks & exit gate": ten Owlshift tickets drained serially by `owlshift watch --drain`, at least one started by the merge of its blocker, run by the maintainer and recorded in the build plan as P2's and P3's gates were.

## Acceptance

* What the build plan's part L lists is built and tested, and matches [architecture](<https://github.com/pitchopp/owlshift/blob/main/docs/design/architecture.md>) section 5, "The drain".
* Any deviation from the design starts with a change to the design documents.

## Links

* [Build plan](<https://github.com/pitchopp/owlshift/blob/main/docs/design/build-plan.md>), "P4 · The drain", "Who builds what", part L; and "P4 tasks & exit gate".
* [Architecture](<https://github.com/pitchopp/owlshift/blob/main/docs/design/architecture.md>), section 5, "The drain".
